_comment: Ireland quiz bank. Option index 'answer' is the correct one; options are shuffled at play time.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Ireland?
questions.fact: Dublin (Baile Átha Cliath) has been Ireland's capital for centuries.

questions.q: Which is Ireland's longest river?
questions.fact: The Shannon runs about 360 km from Cavan to the Atlantic below Limerick.

questions.q: Ireland's highest mountain is…
questions.fact: Carrauntoohil in Kerry's MacGillycuddy's Reeks is 1,039 m high.

questions.q: How many provinces does Ireland have?
questions.fact: Leinster, Munster, Connacht and Ulster.

questions.q: Ireland's largest lake is…
questions.fact: Lough Neagh in the north is the biggest lake on the island.

questions.q: The Cliffs of Moher are in which county?
questions.fact: They rise over 200 m above the Atlantic near Doolin.

questions.q: Which plant is a symbol of Ireland?
questions.fact: Saint Patrick is said to have used its three leaves to explain the Trinity.

questions.q: Saint Patrick's Day is on…
questions.fact: It is Ireland's national holiday.

questions.q: What currency is used in the Republic of Ireland?
questions.fact: The euro replaced the Irish punt in 2002.

questions.q: Which GAA sport uses a sliotar?
questions.fact: A sliotar is the small leather ball; camogie uses one too.

questions.q: Croke Park is in which city?
questions.fact: It holds over 82,000 people and is the GAA's headquarters.

questions.q: Where is the Book of Kells kept?
questions.fact: The 9th-century manuscript is displayed in the Old Library.

questions.q: The Titanic was built in…
questions.fact: Harland & Wolff built her; she last called at Cobh in 1912.

questions.q: Which county is called the Garden of Ireland?
questions.fact: Home to Powerscourt, Glendalough and the Wicklow Mountains.

questions.q: Ireland's smallest county is…
questions.fact: Louth is called the Wee County.

questions.q: Ireland's largest county is…
questions.fact: Cork is known as the Rebel County.

questions.q: Newgrange is in which county?
questions.fact: The passage tomb is older than Stonehenge and the pyramids of Giza.

questions.q: The Giant's Causeway is in which county?
questions.fact: Legend says Finn McCool built it to reach Scotland.

questions.q: How do you say hello in Irish?
questions.fact: It literally means 'God be with you'.

questions.q: What is the Irish word for water?
questions.fact: Whiskey comes from 'uisce beatha', the water of life.

questions.q: Who wrote Ulysses?
questions.fact: The novel follows Leopold Bloom around Dublin on 16 June 1904.

questions.q: Which Irish poet won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1995?
questions.fact: Heaney was born in Co. Derry.

questions.q: W. B. Yeats is buried in which county?
questions.fact: His grave at Drumcliffe lies under Ben Bulben.

questions.q: What is Dublin's tram system called?
questions.fact: Luas is the Irish word for speed.

questions.q: What are the letters of Ireland's national broadcaster?
questions.fact: Raidió Teilifís Éireann.

questions.q: What is the head of the Irish Government called?
questions.fact: The Tánaiste is the deputy.

questions.q: Where does the President of Ireland live?
questions.fact: It stands in the Phoenix Park.

questions.q: Ireland's oldest city is…
questions.fact: Founded by Vikings in 914.

questions.q: The Aran Islands are off which county?
questions.fact: Inis Mór, Inis Meáin and Inis Oírr.

questions.q: Skellig Michael is off which county?
questions.fact: Its beehive huts appeared in Star Wars.

questions.q: Which river flows through Cork city?
questions.fact: The city centre sits on an island in the Lee.

questions.q: Which river flows through Dublin?
questions.fact: The Dodder and Tolka are Dublin rivers too, but the Liffey is the big one.

questions.q: Croagh Patrick is in which county?
questions.fact: Pilgrims climb 'the Reek' on the last Sunday of July.

questions.q: What are the colours of the Irish flag, in order?
questions.fact: Green for the Gaelic tradition, orange for the followers of William of Orange, white for peace.

questions.q: Which instrument appears on Irish euro coins?
questions.fact: The harp has been Ireland's emblem for centuries.

questions.q: Which city is the City of the Tribes?
questions.fact: Named after the 14 merchant families who ran the town.

questions.q: Kilkenny is most famous for which sport?
questions.fact: The Cats have won the Liam MacCarthy Cup many times.

questions.q: Donegal is in which province?
questions.fact: Three Ulster counties are in the Republic: Donegal, Cavan and Monaghan.

questions.q: Kerry is in which province?
questions.fact: Munster also includes Cork, Clare, Limerick, Tipperary and Waterford.

questions.q: Galway is in which province?
questions.fact: Connacht is the western province.

questions.q: Dublin is in which province?
questions.fact: Leinster has twelve counties.

questions.q: What is Tír na nÓg?
questions.fact: Oisín rode there with Niamh on a white horse.

questions.q: Who is known as the Hound of Ulster?
questions.fact: As a boy he was called Setanta.

questions.q: The Children of Lir were turned into…
questions.fact: They spent 900 years as swans.

questions.q: Fungie, who lived in Dingle harbour, was a…
questions.fact: He arrived in 1983 and stayed for decades.

questions.q: Which ancient festival became Halloween?
questions.fact: Samhain marked the end of the harvest and the start of winter.

questions.q: How many times has Ireland won the Eurovision Song Contest?
questions.fact: More than any other country, including three in a row from 1992 to 1994.

questions.q: The Spire stands on which Dublin street?
questions.fact: It is 120 m tall.

questions.q: How many counties are on the island of Ireland?
questions.fact: 26 in the Republic and 6 in Northern Ireland.

questions.q: What is the Dáil?
questions.fact: TDs sit in Dáil Éireann at Leinster House.

questions.q: Molly Malone sold…
questions.fact: 'Alive, alive-oh!' Her statue is on Suffolk Street.

questions.q: Which county is nicknamed The Kingdom?
questions.fact: Kerry has won more All-Ireland football titles than anyone.

questions.q: The Sam Maguire Cup is awarded in…
questions.fact: The hurling equivalent is the Liam MacCarthy Cup.

questions.q: Limerick is nicknamed…
questions.fact: After the Treaty of Limerick of 1691.

questions.q: The Rock of Cashel is in which county?
questions.fact: It was the seat of the Kings of Munster.

questions.q: Which Irish saint's cross is woven from rushes?
questions.fact: Saint Brigid's Day, 1 February, is now a public holiday.

questions.q: What does 'Slán' mean?
questions.fact: Slán go fóill means 'bye for now'.

questions.q: Which county is known as the Rebel County?
questions.fact: The name goes back to the 1490s.

questions.q: Which Irish city is called the Marble City?
questions.fact: Its dark limestone polishes like marble.

questions.q: Bunratty Castle is in which county?
questions.fact: It stands near Shannon Airport.
